subject: Usage-signal driven GPU repointing and flexible buffer for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Cooper Nguyen <cooper.nguyen@arcadialabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Usage signals + renewal — suggested repointing and buffer

Hi Cooper —

Thanks again for the time last week. We ran the utilization analysis on your Dedicated pool for Feb and pulled together a short recommendation for your upcoming renewal. Key takeaways in the attached CSV: overall utilization ran ~68% on average, but there were three short multi-day spikes that pushed effective concurrency and queueing on the small-model lane.

Quick proposal (high level):
- Convert 8% of the committed GPUs from general-purpose slots to a small-model-optimized tranche (shorter sequences, higher throughput).
- Add a temporary 10% flexible buffer (reserved but billable only when used) to absorb bursty experiments while you finalize batching/kv-cache improvements.
- Keep the existing quantization profile; we don’t recommend re-quantizing mid-term.

I've attached the utilization export (arcadia_utilization_feb2028.csv) and a simple sizing worksheet (proposed_commit_change_v1.xlsx) showing throughput impact. Would you be available for a short 30-min ops call on Monday to walk the numbers and, if it looks good, kick off an SOW amendment?

If you'd like, we can also show a simulated cost delta for the buffer usage vs. a pure-commit increase.

Thanks —
Jonas

Jonas Weber
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0123

On a side note: looping in Karthik and Marissa for capacity and SOW coordination.
From: Cooper Nguyen <cooper.nguyen@arcadialabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage signals + renewal — suggested repointing and buffer

Jonas —

Appreciate the quick analysis and the attachments — looked through the CSV and the worksheet. A few clarifying items from our side before we commit to a call:

1) Those multi-day spikes — were they tied to a single job type (training-style evals) or production inference? We ran a large batch of in-house A/B evaluations on Feb 18–20 which might explain the tail.
2) If we accept the 10% flexible buffer, what’s the billing model? Is it usage-based at on-demand rates, or a pro-rated commit?
3) Any risk the tranche reallocation will increase latency for our long-context models? We can't afford regressions on the critical workflows.

If you can answer those in a reply, we can confirm a Monday 10:00am PT slot.

Thanks —
Cooper

Cooper Nguyen
Head of Platform
Arcadia Labs
cooper.nguyen@arcadialabs.com | +1-650-555-4310
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Cooper Nguyen <cooper.nguyen@arcadialabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage signals + renewal — suggested repointing and buffer

Cooper —

Great questions, quick answers below and then I’ll plan to demonstrate on Monday: 

1) Spike attribution: good catch — the Feb 18–20 event is responsible for one of the spikes. The other two spikes are short-lived production experiments (feature-launch A/B traffic) where concurrency ramped for ~6–12 hours each. I’ve flagged rows in the CSV with the job_type column where it’s clearly internal eval vs production traffic.

2) Billing model for the 10% flexible buffer: this would be a reserved buffer on the contract but billable at a reduced overage rate (we propose 40% of on-demand price) and only charged for the hours it’s consumed. The benefit is you get capacity guarantees for bursts without a full commit. We’ll include exact numbers in the SOW appendix and walk through cost simulations on the call.

3) Latency risk for long-context models: re-pointing 8% into a small-model tranche is non-invasive. We’d deploy the small-model tranche on separate instance types tuned for shorter-sequence throughput; long-context instances remain unchanged. If you prefer, we can route via policy (latency-first routing for critical routes) so there is zero impact to those workflows.

Attached: a slightly updated worksheet with scenario rows for buffer utilization and the estimated delta to monthly spend.

If Monday 10:00am PT works, I’ll set up a 30-min call and include our Solutions Engineer to show projected tail-latency numbers.

— Jonas

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Cooper Nguyen <cooper.nguyen@arcadialabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 16:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage signals + renewal — suggested repointing and buffer

Cooper / Jonas —

Thanks for the quick back-and-forth. After reviewing the worksheet and the utilization CSV, ops is comfortable with the proposed approach. Two operational commitments from our side: 

- We will reserve a 10% flexible buffer on the renewal as a billed-but-only-if-used tranche. As Jonas noted, the overage rate will be set at 40% of on-demand in the SOW appendix.
- We’ll reallocate 8% of the committed GPUs into a small-model-optimized pool and ensure routing policies keep long-context workloads pinned to the existing tranche. We’ll also add an observability dashboard row for queueing to detect regressions within the first 14 days after change.

Action items: 
1) Marissa — please draft the amendment (SOW addendum + pricing appendix) and include the buffer billing language; use deal id DL-87342-ARC.
2) Neha — please prepare the DocuSign envelope for client signature and add the HubSpot deal link.
3) Ben — can you confirm the SLA clause for burst capacity (we'll propose a 99.5% instance-ready SLA for buffer usage)?

Cooper — if the above aligns with you, we’ll send the amendment and a DocuSign link by EOD Monday once we finalize the short call and confirm numbers.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions & Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0199
